sentence: A troponin test measures proteins released when heart muscle is damaged, and a raised result does not always mean a heart attack.
note: MedlinePlus: troponin released when heart muscle damaged; NHS: raised troponin may have other causes

sentence: Troponin T and troponin I are proteins found in heart muscle.
They are released into the blood when the heart muscle is damaged, for example in a heart attack.
The more damage there is, the more troponin reaches the blood.
The NHS says troponin is the protein doctors most commonly measure in blood tests for heart damage.
note: added after second pass: Troponin is the most common protein measurement that doctors check

sentence: Clinicians mainly use the test to check whether a heart attack is happening or has recently happened.
It is typically ordered when someone has chest pain or other signs of a heart attack.
An NHS laboratory describes troponin as also helping to predict short-term and longer-term outcomes in acute coronary syndrome.
The NHS treats an ECG as an important early test in a suspected heart attack, and says it should be done within 10 minutes of arrival at hospital.
Blood tests look for troponin, which leaks slowly into the blood after damage to the heart.
Levels usually rise over hours, so testing is often repeated over several hours.
NICE describes taking a second troponin sample after the first, with timing that depends on the test and the first result.
note: NHS (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: High-sensitivity tests can detect much smaller amounts of troponin than older tests.
note: MedlinePlus (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: MedlinePlus says normal levels hours after symptoms start make a heart attack unlikely, but doctors read results alongside symptoms and the ECG.
note: MedlinePlus (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: Very high levels most often mean a heart attack has occurred.
Raised levels do not always mean a heart attack, because other heart conditions can raise troponin.
A UK study reported by University Hospital Southampton found raised troponin in some people with unrelated conditions, so results need careful interpretation.
After a heart attack, levels may stay high for one to two weeks.
MedlinePlus lists conditions such as an abnormally fast heartbeat, pulmonary hypertension and congestive heart failure as other causes of a raised level.
note: added after second pass: Higher than normal levels may be found in other conditions that damage heart muscle, such as fast heartbeat, pulmonary hypertension, congestive heart failure

sentence: MedlinePlus says a single normal result may be followed by a retest, and a high result usually leads to two or more tests over 24 hours.
note: added after second pass: Because levels change over time, a single normal result may be followed by a retest; high results usually lead to repeat testing over 24 hours

sentence: A Scottish NHS guide says troponin T can stay raised in people with kidney problems or heart failure, so doctors look for a change between samples.
note: added after second pass: Troponin T can be persistently raised (renal impairment, heart failure); diagnosis requires dynamic change

sentence: The Southampton study's lead suggested that the normal cut-off, set using fairly healthy people, may not suit a general hospital population.
note: added after second pass: Cutoff for normal derived from relatively healthy people may not suit a general hospital population

sentence: The ECG and troponin results together help to identify the type of heart attack.
A STEMI shows particular changes on the ECG.
An NSTEMI is found when the ECG does not show those changes but blood tests show heart damage.
The NHS says an ECG is painless and takes about 5 minutes.
note: added after second pass: The test is painless and takes about 5 minutes

sentence: NICE says a STEMI can usually be diagnosed by ECG alone, without waiting for a blood test.
note: added after second pass: STEMI can usually be diagnosed by ECG alone

sentence: The NHS advises calling 999 for chest pain that feels tight or squeezing, or that spreads to the arms, neck or jaw.
The NHS also advises calling 999 for someone who has passed out.
note: NHS (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: The BHF advises calling an ambulance rather than travelling to hospital yourself, because paramedics can start care and tests on the way.
note: NHS (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: The BHF says paramedics can start care and tests, including an ECG, on the way to hospital.
note: added after second pass: Paramedics can start care and tests en route; they typically run an ECG

sentence: NICE recommends high-sensitivity troponin tests as options for ruling out a type of heart attack called NSTEMI in emergency departments.
NICE describes strategies using a single sample on arrival or a second sample after the first, depending on the test and result.
note: NICE (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: A review notes that troponin levels tend to be lower in women than in men because of smaller heart size.
note: NICE (blended summary) | edited after second pass

sentence: Troponin T and troponin I are proteins released into the blood when heart muscle is damaged.
The more damage, the more troponin reaches the blood, and levels rise over hours, so the test is often repeated.
A raised troponin may point to a heart attack, but other conditions can raise it too.
The NHS says to call 999 for chest pain that is tight or squeezing, or that spreads to the arms, neck or jaw.
